title: PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES FOR CENSUS 2027
body_text:
First phase of the Census 2027 i.e., Houselisting and Housing Census has already been completed in 31 States/UTs. In the remaining states first phase of the census is scheduled to be completed by September, 2026. Further, as per the notification dated 3 rd August, 2026 in the Gazette of India, second phase of the Census i.e. Population Enumeration in the UT of Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the UT of Jammu & Kashmir and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the States of Himachal Pradesh and Uttrakhand shall be undertaken from 1 st September, 2026 to 30 th September, 2026 with a revisional round from 1 st October, 2026 to 5 th October, 2026. There shall also be an option for self-enumeration from 17 th August, 2026 to 31 st August, 2026.
Mobile applications for data collection and other digital platforms, including the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) Portal, have been deployed for the conduct of the first phase of Census 2027. The facility of self-enumeration to the respondents through an online web portal has also been given for the first time in Census. Digital tools for the second phase of the census have been developed.
Training of Master Trainers, Field Trainers, Enumerators, Supervisors etc. for the first phase of Census 2027 has been completed/ in progress, in accordance with the notified schedule, in coordination with the States/ UTs Government.
Till now, a total amount of ₹4102 crore have already been released to States/UTs for training of Census functionaries, manpower assistance, technical infrastructure, payment of honorarium to Census functionaries etc.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that the first phase of Census 2027 (Houselisting and Housing Census) has been completed in 31 States/UTs, with the remaining states expected to finish by September 2026. The second phase (Population Enumeration) for Ladakh and snow-bound areas of J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand will run from 1-30 September 2026, with a revisional round from 1-5 October 2026 and a self-enumeration option from 17-31 August 2026. The Ministry has deployed digital tools including the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) Portal and an online self-enumeration facility, and has released ₹4102 crore to States/UTs for training, manpower, infrastructure and honorarium payments.
enrichment.context: Census 2027 will be India's 16th census and the first digital census, delayed from its usual decennial schedule (last census was in 2011) due to the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent administrative decisions. The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948 and Census Rules, 1990, and is a Union subject under the Seventh Schedule. It is conducted in two phases: Houselisting and Housing Census (collecting data on housing conditions, amenities, and assets) followed by Population Enumeration (collecting demographic, socio-economic, cultural and other particulars of individuals). This edition is notable for the first-time inclusion of caste enumeration alongside the traditional SC/ST categories, and for extensive digitisation through mobile apps and the CMMS portal, replacing the paper-based methods of earlier censuses. Snow-bound and difficult terrain regions like Ladakh, parts of J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand are enumerated on a non-synchronous schedule (conducted at a different time than the rest of the country) due to inaccessibility during winter months. Census data forms the basis for delimitation of constituencies, policy planning, resource allocation, and implementation of welfare schemes, making its timely and accurate conduct significant for governance and public administration.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to Census 2027 in India, consider the following statements: 1. It is being conducted in two phases - Houselisting and Housing Census, followed by Population Enumeration. 2. It is the first census in India to use self-enumeration through an online web portal. 3. The Census is conducted under provisions of the Constitution of India directly, without any separate legislation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Census 2027 follows the traditional two-phase structure (Houselisting/Housing Census and Population Enumeration) and introduces self-enumeration via an online portal for the first time. However, census in India is conducted under the Census Act, 1948, a specific legislation, not directly under constitutional provisions, making statement 3 incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: The second phase of Census 2027, i.e., Population Enumeration, is being conducted on a non-synchronous basis in certain snow-bound areas. This means enumeration in these areas is conducted:
options: Simultaneously with the rest of the country using satellite technology
At a different time than the rest of the country due to accessibility constraints
Only through self-enumeration without field enumerators
By the Ministry of Defence instead of the Registrar General of India
prelims_questions.explanation: Non-synchronous enumeration refers to conducting the census at a different time period in areas like Ladakh, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand's snow-bound regions, since heavy snowfall makes access difficult during the regular census period.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Census 2027 as India's first digital census. Examine the challenges and opportunities associated with digitisation of census operations, including tools like the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) Portal and online self-enumeration.

Census data is fundamental to policy formulation and resource allocation in India. Analyse how delays or inaccuracies in census enumeration, particularly in geographically challenging regions, can affect governance and welfare delivery.
